rationale: The v2 limiter was the founder company's inability to create the regulator-backed governance mandate and binding operator coverage on which demand, recurrence, and defensibility depend. The v4 redesign stops treating that public authority as a founder-owned asset: an appointed controller or prime owns the mandate, lawful basis, coalition, and participant commitments, while the founder supplies a reusable white-label technical and operations module. Production is gated on paid scoped discovery and documentary proof of customer authority and binding participation, reducing speculative build exposure without asserting that any sponsor, partner, right, payment, price, or conversion exists. This changes the customer, paid event, offer, distribution route, control point, dependency, compounding asset, and economics; its commercial viability remains a hypothesis requiring disconfirming evidence.
